title: Elementary-shear interpolation for supported Kummer products
statement:
Fix the finite datum $k,\ell,E,n,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions], with arbitrary $n\geq1$, and the twists $A(r)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $X$ be any $k$-scheme and $c\geq0$. For an ordered tuple $h=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$ of global regular functions on $X$, let $C_h\hookrightarrow X$ be the closed subscheme locally defined by the ideal $(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$, and put $D_a(h)=V(h_a)$ and $W_a(h)=X\setminus D_a(h)$. Using the concrete Kummer classes of [def-pur-frame-class], the localization boundaries of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], and the ordered supported cup product of [def-pur-supported-cup], write
$$K_X(h)=\mathop{\bigcup}_{a=1}^c\partial_{D_a(h)}\kappa_{W_a(h)}(h_a|_{W_a(h)})\in H^{2c}_{C_h}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A(c)),$$
where supported cohomology is [def-pur-support-cohomology]. The product is left-associated; at $c=0$ it is $1\in H^0(X,A)$ with $C_h=X$. This formula uses arbitrary functions, without smoothness, regularity, finite-type or separatedness hypotheses on $X$.

Suppose $c\geq2$, choose distinct indices $i,j$ and $a\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and let $h'$ be obtained by replacing $h_i$ by $h_i+a h_j$ and leaving the other entries fixed. Put $T=\mathbf A^1_X$ with projection $p$, coordinate $t$, and zero and unit sections $s_0,s_1:X\to T$ ([def-sbc-affine-space]). Define $H_b=p^*h_b$ for $b\ne i$ and $H_i=p^*h_i+t(p^*a)(p^*h_j)$. Then $C_{h'}=C_h$ and $C_H=T\times_X C_h$ as closed subschemes. The explicit class
$$\eta=K_T(H)\in H^{2c}_{T\times_X C_h}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A(c))$$
is defined by the same individual-boundary product formula, and satisfies
$$s_0^*\eta=K_X(h),\qquad s_1^*\eta=K_X(h'),\qquad s_0^*\eta=s_1^*\eta.$$
All pullbacks use their inverse-image supports and the canonical twist identifications. Consequently $K_X(h')=K_X(h)$. In particular, on an etale frame neighborhood this gives invariance under a single elementary shear, without requiring $T$ itself to be an etale frame neighborhood.

Agent-formulated auxiliary assertion for the corrected concrete pro-etale finite-coefficient construction; this is not a theorem quoted verbatim from Stacks.

proof.text: On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, write $I=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$. Because $i\ne j$, $h_j$ is unchanged, and $h_i=(h_i+ah_j)-ah_j$. Thus every generator of $I$ belongs to $(h'_1,\ldots,h'_c)$; the reverse inclusion follows from $h'_i=h_i+ah_j$. Hence these ideals are equal, giving $C_{h'}=C_h$ scheme-theoretically. By [def-sbc-affine-space], the inverse image of this open in $T$ is $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$. There the same two inclusions, using $h_i=H_i-taH_j$, give $(H_1,\ldots,H_c)=IR[t]$. The fibre product with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R[t]\otimes_R R/I)=\operatorname{Spec}(R[t]/IR[t])$. These equalities of ideal sheaves agree on overlaps, so $C_H=T\times_X C_h$. No division or reducedness is used.

proof.text: The displayed formula defines a class for any tuple $g_1,\ldots,g_c$ on any $k$-scheme $Y$: on $Y\setminus V(g_b)$ the function $g_b$ has inverse $1/g_b$, so the arbitrary-unit construction in [def-pur-frame-class] gives $\kappa(g_b)$ with the specified finite coefficients for every $n\geq1$. Apply the pro-etale localization boundary of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] to obtain a class of degree $2$ supported on $V(g_b)$. Take their ordered left-associated product using [def-pur-supported-cup]. After the first $b$ factors its support is the closed subscheme with ideal $(g_1,\ldots,g_b)$, its degree is $2b$, and its coefficient is $A(b)$. For the coefficients, [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](3) makes $A(1)$ a locally free rank-one finite sheaf; its finite tensor powers are again locally free, so the derived tensors here are the ordinary tensor powers identified with $A(b)$ by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The initial factor has exactly these properties at $b=1$, and each cup adds one support ideal, degree $2$, and one twist. Thus the formula gives $K_Y(g)$ as stated, with no frame hypothesis. Apply this construction to $Y=T$ and $g=H$; Step 1 places the resulting $\eta$ in the claimed support group. The empty tuple instead gives the specified unit with full support.

source.place: 'Elementary shears': interpolate the equations, keep their total support fixed, and compare t=0 and t=1 by supported affine-line invariance.

proof.text: On every $R[t]$ chart of [def-sbc-affine-space], $s_0$ and $s_1$ are the evaluations $t\mapsto0$ and $t\mapsto1$, and both are the identity on $R$. Therefore $s_0^*H_b=h_b$ for all $b$, while $s_1^*H_b=h'_b$ for all $b$. Pulling back a principal ideal $(H_b)$ along these ring maps gives $(h_b)$ or $(h'_b)$ respectively; hence the individual divisors and their open complements pull back to the corresponding endpoint divisors and complements. Pulling back the total ideal $IR[t]$ gives $I$ at either endpoint, so both total inverse-image supports are $C_h$, with the second also identified with $C_{h'}$ by Step 1.

source.place: 'Elementary shears': interpolate the equations, keep their total support fixed, and compare t=0 and t=1 by supported affine-line invariance.

proof.text:
For $\epsilon=0,1$ put $g^{(0)}=h$ and $g^{(1)}=h'$. For each $b$, restrict $s_\epsilon$ to the inverse-image open complement from Step 3. The Kummer naturality and localization-boundary compatibility of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] give
$$s_\epsilon^*\bigl(\partial_{V(H_b)}\kappa(H_b)\bigr)=\partial_{V(g^{(\epsilon)}_b)}\kappa(g^{(\epsilon)}_b).$$
Here each Kummer class is taken on its own open complement, and every boundary has degree $1\to2$ with twist $A(1)$. To pass to the ordered products, start with this equality for the first factor. If it holds for the product of the first $b$ factors, the cup-pullback identity of the same cited node applies to that degree-$2b$, twist-$b$ class and the next degree-$2$, twist-$1$ class, proving it for $b+1$. This finite induction keeps the original left association and uses no permutation or sign change. Consequently $s_0^*\eta=K_X(h)$ and $s_1^*\eta=K_X(h')$, in the common supported group of Step 3. The cited naturality assertions hold on the pro-etale site for arbitrary morphisms of $k$-schemes and the concrete coefficients used here.

source.place: 'Elementary shears': interpolate the equations, keep their total support fixed, and compare t=0 and t=1 by supported affine-line invariance.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-supported-affine-line-homotopy] with its base $X$, closed subscheme $C=C_h$, degree $q=2c$, and twist $r=c$. Its hypotheses allow arbitrary $k$-schemes and every $n\geq1$, so they apply to the present data. Its specific projection pullback $p^*$ is an isomorphism, and its statement says that both section pullbacks are its inverse, with inverse-image support $C_h$. Thus $s_0^*\eta=s_1^*\eta$. Combining with Step 4 gives $K_X(h)=K_X(h')$, hence the claimed invariance. An etale frame neighborhood is a particular $k$-scheme with such a tuple; applying the same argument there proves the last assertion. At no point is the interpolation space $T$ required to be an etale frame neighborhood.
